data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Hanan means "grace, favor, compassion, loving-kindness, and mercy". In the Bible, there is a woman named Hannah who was barren and prayed to God for a child. God answered her prayer, and she named her son Samuel, which means "asked of God". This name is a reminder of God's grace and mercy towards us in answering our prayers.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes the boundless grace and mercy of God towards us.
data.etymology: Hannia belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Grace, Mercy, Favor.”

in_hebrew.name: חניה
in_hebrew.meaning: חניה - חסד אלוהים, חנן על ידי אלוהים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: חניה הוא שם עברי שמשמעותו 'חסד אלוהים' או 'חנן על ידי אלוהים'. השם מורכב משתי מילים: 'חנ-' שפירושה 'חסד' או 'חנינה', ו'-יה' שפירושו 'אלוהים'. השם חניה מופיע בתנ"ך מספר פעמים, ביניהם בספר נחמיה, שם מוזכר חניה בן עזריהו, אחד מהשרים ששירתו תחת המלך יאשיהו. השם חניה נושא משמעות רבה בחברה היהודית והנוצרית כאחד, והוא מבטא את הרעיון של חסד אלוהים והאהבה האלוהית.

in_greek.name: Χαννία
in_greek.meaning: Χαννία - ἡ χάρις τοῦ θεοῦ, χαριζόμενος ὑπὸ θεοῦ
in_greek.long_meaning: Χαννία είναι ένα ελληνικό όνομα που προέρχεται από την εβραϊκή γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'η χάρις τοῦ θεοῦ' (η χάρη του Θεού) ή 'χαριζόμενος ὑπὸ θεοῦ' (χαριζόμενος από τον Θεό). Το όνομα Χαννία απαντάται στη Βίβλο, συγκεκριμένα στη Καινή Διαθήκη, όπου αναφέρεται ο Χαννίας, ένας από τους μαθητές του Ιησού Χριστού. Το όνομα Χαννία έχει μεγάλη σημασία στην χριστιανική παράδοση και συμβολίζει τη χάρη και την αγάπη του Θεού.

in_latin.name: Hannia
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Hannia derivatum est ex lingua hebraica et significat 'gratia Dei' vel 'donum Dei'. Nomen hoc in Biblia saepius occurrit, inter alia in libro Nehemiae, ubi commemoratur Hannia filius Azariae, unus ex principibus qui servierunt sub rege Josia. Nomen Hannia in traditione christiana et judaica magnam habet significationem et exprimit gratiam et amorem divinum.

in_english.name: Hannia
in_english.meaning: Gracious, favored by God, gift of God
in_english.long_meaning: The name Hannia originates from the Hebrew language, specifically from the words 'chana,' meaning 'grace' or 'favor,' and 'Yah,' referring to God. Thus, Hannia can be interpreted as 'gracious,' 'favored by God,' or 'gift of God.' This name appears several times in the Bible, including in the book of Nehemiah, where Hannia, son of Azariah, is mentioned as one of the officials under King Josiah. In Christian tradition, the name Hannia symbolizes divine grace and love. It reflects the qualities of being gracious, compassionate, and spiritually gifted. The name has been used across various Christian cultures, maintaining its significance and spiritual connotation.

She is said to have been a young girl who was martyred during the Roman Emperor Diocletian's persecution of Christians around AD 304. Her relics were later transferred to Constantinople, and she is now venerated as a saint in the Eastern Orthodox Church.
